content: IMB Graphic NASHVILLE – As the books closed on the latest fiscal year, receipts for the two Southern Baptist national annual missions offerings underscored the value Southern Baptist churches place on reaching the world with the gospel. The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. For some it is a few hundred dollars, for others several thousand.” The Annie Armstrong offering supports more than 3,000 missionaries in North America, including the ongoing work of church planting in the U.S. and Canada. In 2025, Southern Baptists planted the largest number of churches, 699, since 2016. Including church plants and replants, Southern Baptists have surpassed 700 new churches in four of the last five years. More than 12,000 churches have been planted since 2010. The five consecutive years of increase marked the first such streak in approximately 75 years. summary_zh: 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教会实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划
title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州浸信会加入派遣教会实验室，以加强传教士支持
content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. From a missionary perspective, she believes the lab addresses a common challenge. “It’s hard to know sometimes as churches how to be a good sending church and how to support missionaries,” she sa
content_zh: 俄克拉何马州瓦戈纳第一浸信会的工作人员评价了教会参与传教和传教活动的情况。 IMB 相片 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教士实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划,其中心是一个问题: 教会真正成为送教之所意味着什么? 对于俄克拉何马浸信会的全球使命部合作伙伴迈克·沃尔来说,答案始于教会重新为大委员会负责。 去年沃尔在图尔萨参加了一个送教实验室, 他离开后确信更多的教会需要训练. “当我去那里时,我想,`你必须在俄克拉荷马城做这件事,'墙说,`因为内容和我们的教会需要这样的东西。 在观察了教堂通过实验室的演练工作后,沃尔说,他在任务中强调当地教会的所有权使他受到鼓舞. “我们不能只是派我们的人来说,“好吧,这是你的工作,IMB。” “我们必须在派遣、准备和训练最优秀的`派遣 ' 人员方面完成我们的工作,这样,当他们到达实地时,他们就已经可以奔跑地了。” Bryan Wooten,IMB高级教会订婚专家,在俄克拉荷马城的Constitution Road Baptist教堂领导一个送教实验室. 他强调派遣教会评估和装备未来的IMB传教士的重要性. IMB Photo Leading the lab是IMB高级教会接触策略师布莱恩·伍滕(Bryan Wooten),他在看到传教士与本地教会之间需要更牢固的关系后发展出这个概念. 伍腾说,“一个派遣教会实验室是我们努力培养许多派遣教会的IMB。 ”他赞扬北美传教委员会开展了类似的活动并取得了成功。 实验室帮助教会理解伍腾所谓的教会参与途径:祈祷,合作,合作和发送. 虽然许多教堂忠实地祈祷,奉献和去,但他说送去需要更有意图的东西. 他解释说,“最后包括负责一个IMB传教士,在整个任职期间提供持续的鼓励、问责和精神关怀。” 在为期两天的活动期间,与会者聚集在白板周围,评价其教会的任务做法,查明优缺点并制订改进计划。 」伍腾说: “我们需要邀请教会自己做一些工作。” 与会者不是简单地听取演讲,而是通过祷告、赠送、短期访问、传教士评估和长期照料等实际问题开展工作。 Wooten说,教会总是告诉他最大的好处是清晰. 他说,“他们感谢对派遣教会的咨监委的澄清,以及我们的作用和责任。” 对于IMB的传教士彼得和凯蒂·威克斯来说,这种清晰度特别有价值. 他们与教会领袖一起参加了实验室. 他们的真名被更改以保护自己在东南亚的工作. 彼得说,“在这几天里,我宁愿呆在这里。” 凯蒂对培训的互动性表示赞赏. 我非常欣赏他们要求不同教会提供信息的方式, 从传教士的角度来看,她认为实验室解决了共同的挑战. " 作为教会,有时很难知道 如何成为一个好的送信教会 以及如何支持传教士,"
author: Chris Doyle

title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
summary_zh: 北中央省
title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.
content_zh:
2013年5月哈萨克斯坦逮捕Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev牧师时,他是一位老人。 指控是奇怪的,他伤害了一名教会成员的健康并煽动了宗教仇恨。 他们判处他十年监禁,并把他关进精神病病房,囚犯经常在那里服药。 进来的路上,他觉得这也许是他心智的终结.

"这可能是我最后一次在正确的思想中和你说话,"他说. 然后,一个问题来到他身上,神用的那种。 "你的信仰在哪里?" 在升起的上帝的掩护下 有东西解除了 "我觉得自己在升天主的掩护下,"他说. 期待失去自我的老人却发现耶稣比墙壁更靠近. 他开始和周围的人交谈

对一个吸毒成瘾的囚犯来说 他只是说 只有耶稣才能帮助你 里面有九个月,近一百名囚犯为基督献出了生命。 "在狱中",他说"圣灵为我打开了祈祷的一个维度". 打算打破他的地方成为了他一生中最有成果的支点. 他们于2014年初释放了他。

他走了出去 埋下了好消息 在最后的地方 没有人会寻找它。 上帝不会被任何锁住你的门锁住 他已经在里面等了

title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱

title: He survived the killing fields. Then he baptised the man who ran a death camp
summary: 🇰🇭Cambodia· 1980s-1990s
title_zh: 他从“杀戮之地”幸存下来。后来，他为一名曾经营死亡集中营的人施洗。
content: Christopher LaPel grew up near the royal palace in Cambodia and wore a small ivory cross as a boy, though his father disapproved. Then the Khmer Rouge came. In 1975 he was driven into the labour camps, working sixteen-hour days in the fields. He lost both parents, a brother, and a sister to execution and starvation. He nearly died himself. When he was too sick to work for three days, soldiers came to execute him, and one of them looked at him and said he really looks sick, and walked away. He survived into a refugee camp in Thailand, empty and grieving. There a missionary told him that Jesus Christ had died on the cross for his sins. "This is the answer I've been waiting for," LaPel said, and he gave Jesus his life. The general who said, my sin is so deep LaPel became a pastor and went back to teach his own people. In 1995 a quiet man calling himself Hang Pin came to one of his leadership trainings. He gave his life to Christ, was baptised the next day, and began leading a house church. Only later did the world learn who he really was. Kang Kek Iew, known as Comrade Duch, had run S-21, the prison where around twelve thousand people were tortured and killed. He came to LaPel and said, "My sin is so deep." Duch surrendered to the authorities and was sentenced to life in prison, where he wore out the Bibles LaPel kept sending him. The man who survived the killing fields carried the grace of Jesus back to one of the men who built them. No sin is too deep for the blood of Jesus. Not the worst thing done to you. Not the worst thing you have done.
content_zh:
克里斯托弗·拉佩尔(Christopher LaPel)在柬埔寨的皇家宫殿附近长大并作为一个男孩穿小象牙十字架,尽管他的父亲不赞成. 后来红色高棉来了. 1975年,他被驱入劳改营,在田地工作了16小时. 他的父母、兄弟和姐妹都死于处决和饥饿。 他差点死了

当他生病了三天不能工作时,士兵们来处决他,其中一人看着他,说他真的病了,走了. 他活了下来,进入了泰国的一个难民营,空虚而悲伤. 有一个传教士告诉他,耶稣基督因他的罪而死于十字架上. 拉佩尔说:"这就是我一直在等待的答案",他给了耶稣一命.

将军说,我的罪恶是如此之深拉佩尔成为牧师,回去教自己的人. 1995年,一个叫作"杭平"的安静人来到了自己的领导训练之一. 他把生命献给基督,第二天被洗礼,并开始领导一所房屋教堂. 直到后来,世界才知道他的真实身份.

姜克毅被称作"杜克同志",曾经营过S-21监狱,当时大约有一万二千人被拷打并杀害. 他来到拉佩尔说:"我的罪恶是如此之深". 杜克向当局自首并被判处终身监禁,在那里他穿了"圣经"LaPel继续送去.

在杀戮地中幸存下来的人将耶稣的恩典带回了建造他们的人之一. 没有罪过是太深 对于耶稣的血。 不是对你最坏的事 不是你做过的最坏的事

title: A witch doctor got a solar radio. It was tuned to the truth
summary: 🇨🇬Democratic Republic of Congo· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇨🇬刚果民主共和国·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 巫医有一台太阳能收音机。它被调到了真相频道
content: Mbutu was a witch doctor in a remote village in the Democratic Republic of Congo. For years he cast spells, claimed power over the natural world, and sold cures to sick villagers who had nowhere else to turn. People feared him. He made his living off that fear. Then he was given a small solar-powered radio. It was fixed to one station, a local Christian broadcast, and handed out to villagers who had no other way to hear anything. Tuned to the truth So Mbutu listened. Day after day the good news came through that little speaker. He learned of the One who really controls the universe, and more than that, he learned about the love of Jesus and His offer of forgiveness. The man who had traded in fear laid his witchcraft down and gave his life to Christ. He did not keep it to himself. Mbutu now walks from village to village, finding other witch doctors and telling them what he found. Some of them have become believers. Some have become pastors, planting churches where there were none. A cheap radio and the name of Jesus were enough to turn the most feared man in the village into its brightest light. No one is beyond the reach of that name. Not the person others are afraid of. Not you.
content_zh:
Mbutu是刚果民主共和国一个偏远村庄的一名巫医。 多年来,他施了咒语,声称对自然世界拥有权力,并出售给没有别处可转的病村民的治疗方法. 人们害怕他。 他靠恐惧为生 后被给予小型太阳能收音机.

它被固定在一个电台,一个当地的基督教广播,并交给没有其他办法听到任何消息的村民. 实话实说 姆博图听了 日复一日的好消息从那个小演讲者那里传来。 他得知了真正控制宇宙之人,不止于此,他还了解到了耶稣的爱和他提出的宽恕.

在恐惧中交易的人放下了巫术,将他的生命献给了基督. 他没有保守秘密。 姆布图现在从村到村走来走去,找到其他巫医,并告诉他们他发现了什么. 他们中有一部分已变成信士。 有些人成为牧师,在没有教堂的地方种植教堂。

一个廉价的收音机和耶稣的名字足以将村里最被敬畏的人变成最明亮的光芒. 没有人能够超越这个名字。 不是别人害怕的人 不是你,你没有

summary_zh: 能够与Missionary合作，创作面向儿童的图画传记系列《Goers》，我深感荣幸。每本传记都向年轻的读者和听众讲述那些被教会派出去将耶稣基督的福音传到地极的男男女女的故事。另请参阅今日出版：埃里克最伟大的比赛6本适合儿童的优秀新书约翰·加尔文（适合青少年读者的基督教人物传记）
title_zh: 教导子女了解那些被差遣的人
content: It was a great honor to be able to partner with Missionary to create Goers , a series of illustrated biographies for children. Each biography introduces young readers and listeners to the stories of men and women who were sent by churches to spread the good news about Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. Each is illustrated by the ultra-talented Rommel Ruiz. The books can be purchased as a set of three or as individual volumes. The Plowboy’s Bible: The Story of William Tyndale’s English Translation . Hunted by spies, William Tyndale fled across Europe with a bounty on his head, his Bible translation labeled as contraband. Young John, on the other hand, has a long day of farm work ahead of him. Although their lives seem worlds apart, John’s father knows a story that binds John and William together—their love for God’s word. The scripture John relies on for encouragement cost William everything, but they gave John’s family everything! Rescued from Darkness: Amy Carmichael and the Girls of Dohnavur . Kumari is scared, helpless, and alone in a dark temple until Amma, a mysterious woman from a faraway land, carries her away to a beautiful garden. This is not a fairy tale. It’s the true story of missionary Amy Carmichael and the children she rescued and raised at Dohnavur Fellowship in India. Into the Unknown: David Livingstone’s Heart for Africa . Before David Livingstone was the most famous man in the world, he was a boy who dreamed of being free to explore God’s creation. But when David reached the mission field, he found that freedom taken from the people he tried to teach about the Creator. This is the story of a goer’s dangerous journey to the ends of the earth, of his courageous stand for justice, and of his patient endurance for the sake of Christ. The Goers series is written for children ages 4–10, and is ideal for parents to read to their children or for young readers to read on their own. Each book includes discussion questions and prayer points to get your family thinking and praying about the Great Commission. Each hardcover volume has 40 full-color pages and is sized 10″ x 10″. The Goers series is currently available exclusively through Westminster Books . Look for three more volumes to be added to the series around this time next year. See Also Releasing Today: Eric’s Greatest Race 6 Great New Books for Kids John Calvin (Christian Biographies for Young Readers)
content_zh:
能够和传教士合作创作Goers, 每部传记都向年轻的读者和听众介绍被教会派去向世界末端传播耶稣基督的好消息的男女的故事. 每个都由超能的隆美尔·鲁伊斯(英语:Rommel Ruiz)来说明.

书籍可作为一套三卷或单卷购买. 《犁男孩的圣经:威廉·廷达勒英文译本的故事》。 在间谍的追捕下,威廉·廷达勒带着头上的赏金逃过欧洲,他的圣经译本标注为违禁品. 而年轻的约翰则有很长的一天的农场工作在他前面.

虽然他们的生活似乎有些不同,但约翰的父亲却知道一个把约翰和威廉联系在一起的故事——他们对上帝之言的爱。 圣经中约翰依靠的鼓励让威廉付出了一切,但他们给了约翰的家人一切! 从黑暗中拯救:艾米·卡迈克尔和多赫纳武尔的少女.

库马里害怕,无助,独自在黑暗的神庙中,直到远方的神秘女子阿玛把她带到美丽的花园. 这不是童话 这是传教士Amy Carmichael和在印度Dohnavur联谊会救起和抚养的孩子的真实故事。 David Livingstone的非洲之心。

在大卫·利文斯通(David Livingstone)是世界上最有名的人之前,他是一个梦想自由探索上帝创造的男孩. 但是当大卫到达任务领域时,他发现自由从那些他试图教导造物主的人身上夺走.

这是一位行者前往地球尽头的危险旅程,他勇敢地站在正义面前,以及他为基督而耐心忍耐的故事。 Goers系列为4–10岁的儿童写作,是父母向子女阅读或年轻读者自己阅读的理想.

每本书都包含讨论问题和祈祷点,以让你的家人思考和祈祷大委员会. 每个硬盖卷有40页全色,大小为10′′×10′′. Goers系列目前完全通过Westminster Books提供。 明年的这个时候再找三卷

content: Good morning. If you have read this site for any length of time, you will know that I am not the kind of person who does hot takes, since I just don’t trust myself to do them well. However, with the Wesley Huff situation developing, I did want to link to what I consider an especially helpful assessment of the matter. You can find that beneath today’s recommended reads. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several volumes in the excellent New Studies in Dogmatics series. You’ll also find books by Jinger Duggar Vuolo, David Mathis, John Piper, and others. I continue to find and highlight hardcover and softcover book deals as part of Amazon’s Pre-Black Friday Book Deals . There are around 80 of them now, many of which are half off or more. Recommended Reading Hot Water and Holy Wonder: Giving Thanks for Ordinary Luxuries. “Every now and then, as I sit in my home library, a sense of awe settles over me—a spirit of wonder at the everyday comforts that surround me.” Trevin Wax celebrates the joy of the ordinary luxuries that God so graciously grants us. Are My Prayers Selfish? Responding to a question from a listener, John Piper explains the difference between prayers that are selfish and those that simply ask for things. “James is saying there is a kind of prayer that treats God like a cuckold. It refers to a husband whose wife is cheating on him. That’s a cuckold. Christians are making God into a cuckold. How? When it says they are praying just to spend it on their passions. The picture is of an unfaithful wife who asked her husband for $50 so she can go down the hall and pay another man to have sex with her. That’s the picture. She’s using prayer to cheat on her husband, God.” When the Heavens Declare: What a Solar Halo Says to a Secular City. Johannesburg was recently the site of a solar halo ( see here for images ). Tim Cantrell writes about what the skies were declaring in that moment. Gospel-Pilling the Looksmaxxers: Hope for Despairing Men. “What do dating apps, the 1999 film The Matrix, rhinoplasty, crystal meth, and smashing your face with a hammer all have in common? Welcome to the world of looksmaxxers. Let’s start at the beginning.” Mark Sanders introduces a concerning trend for young men and offers a much more satisfying hope. Here Are the Lessons I’ve Learned About Single Missionaries (From a Lifetime of Being One). I’m neither single nor a missionary, but still very much appreciate Andy Smith’s thoughts on the matter. “I always assumed that I would get married. I never thought I would enter full-time ministry. Yet, here I am, a contented single missionary since 1989.” Don’t Be Afraid to Provoke Your Brothers. Michael Kelley says why it’s important that we provoke one another. “I grew up in a house with two brothers. By the time we were all in school, ‘provoking’ was down to an art form. For each of my brothers, I knew the right buttons to push to get a rise out of them. I knew the words, the facial expressions, or even the subtle hint to drop that would flush their anger. What’s more, I knew how to do it to one of them to get at the other one. Like I said, an art form.” On Wesley Huff All those who have heard the recent news about Wesley Huff’s plagiarism have been shocked by it, myself no less than anyone else. I think Glen Scrivener is especially helpful, firm, and compassionate in this video . Even if you don’t watch it all, consider watching the final 10 minutes for the brief “sermon” he preaches there. Huff released a statement yesterday, which you can read on X or Facebook . Flashback The Blessing of a Higher Purpose in Our Pain. The chief end of affliction is to glorify God and enjoy him. The purpose of our lives is the purpose of our times of struggle, loss, grief, illness, and bereavement. The local church enables the world to look upon the canvas of God’s people and see an authentic painting of Christ’s love and holiness, not a forgery. —Jonathan Leeman Download Share See Also A La Carte (April 1) A L
content_zh:
早报. 如果你读过这个网站有一段时间, 你会知道,我不是那种热心的人, 因为我不相信自己能做得很好。 然而,随着Wesley Huff局势的发展,我确实想把我认为对此事特别有益的评估联系起来。 在今天推荐的读物中,

今天的销售和交易包括Dogmatics系列优秀新研究的几卷。 你也会找到Jinger Duggar Vuolo、David Mathis、John Piper等人的书。 我继续寻找和强调硬封面和软封面书交易, 现在大约有80种,其中许多是一半或更多。

推荐阅读热水与神圣神奇:为普通的Luxuries致谢. “每当我坐在家里的图书馆里时, 一种敬畏感会安顿在我身上, 特雷文·瓦克斯(Trevin Wax)庆祝上帝如此慷慨赐予我们的普通豪华的喜悦. 我的祷告是自私的吗?

约翰·皮珀(John Piper)在回答一个听众的提问时,解释了自私的祷告和单纯要求事物的祈祷之间的区别. “詹姆斯说,有一种祷告将上帝当作一个笑柄。 它指的是妻子在欺骗他的丈夫。 那是个骗局。 基督徒正在让上帝变成傻瓜 怎么会?

当它说他们祈祷 仅仅把它花在他们的激情。 照片是一位不忠的妻子,她向丈夫索要50美元,这样她就可以下堂,付钱给另一个男人和她做爱. 这张照片就是这样。 她利用祈祷欺骗她的丈夫上帝。 当天堂宣布:太阳光环对世俗城市说些什么.

约翰内斯堡是太阳光环的所在地(图片请参见这里)。 蒂姆·坎特雷尔写了 那一刻天空在宣布什么 (原始内容存档于2018-09-22). Glass-Pilling the Looksmaxxers:希望绝望的人. “约会应用,1999年的电影《母体》,犀角成形术,水晶冰毒,用锤子砸你的脸,有什么共同点? 欢迎来到美容师的世界

让我们从头开始。 马克·桑德斯介绍了青年男子的趋势,并带来了更令人满意的希望。 我所学到的关于单一传教士的教训, 我既不是单身,也不是传教士,但仍非常欣赏安迪·史密斯对此问题的想法. “我一直认为我会结婚。

我从未想过我会进入全职部门 然而,我在这里,是一个自1989年以来满足的单一传教士。” 不要害怕为你的兄弟们辩护。 Michael Kelley指出, “我与两个兄弟在一个房子里长大。 到我们全校时, " 挑衅 " 已沦为艺术形式。

对于我每个兄弟,我都知道正确的按钮 来推动他们起来。 我知道这些话,面部表情, 甚至是会冲动他们的愤怒的微妙暗示。 更何况,我知道如何去对付他们中的一个,

如我所说,艺术形式。” 韦斯利・赫夫 所有听到最近有关Wesley Huff盗版主义的消息的人, 我认为Glen Scrivenner在这段视频中特别有帮助、坚定和同情心。 想想看最后10分钟,

Huff昨天发布了一份声明, 我们痛苦中崇高的祝福 苦难的主要结局是颂扬上帝,享受他. 我们生活的目的,是我们奋斗,损失,悲伤,疾病,丧命的时代的目的.

title_zh: 您愿意考虑支持我的工作吗？
content: I have been blogging at Challies.com on a daily basis for over 23 years now. That long commitment has allowed me to write thousands of articles and hundreds of book reviews while also sending millions of visitors to other sites through the daily A La Carte feature. Though I’ve also written a number of books, the blog has always remained the “main thing.” Much of the blog’s content is now also translated into Spanish , French , and a number of other languages. One of my great desires has always been to freely give away as much as possible. I intend for it to always remain entirely free for all who visit . While, for obvious reasons, this can’t happen when it comes to books, I’ve made it my goal to ensure that everything else has been freely and widely distributed. While this has been possible largely because of advertisers, there is also a key role for the generosity of individuals. This is where patrons come in—patrons like you. There are a couple of different options for you to consider. The first is recurring monthly gifts. A service called Patreon provides a convenient means of linking content producers (like me) with ongoing supporters (like you). You can learn more and sign up at Patreon.com/challies . I also share monthly ministry and family updates there. The second is one-time gifts. If that is of interest to you, they can be made electronically via PayPal . If you prefer to send a one-time gift via check, you can simply mail a check (drawn on a US or Canadian bank) to this address: Tim Challies 1011 Upper Middle Road East, Box #1214 Oakville, Ontario L6H 5Z9 Canada Funds donated will be used to support my family and to help create great content or to otherwise improve, support, and enhance Challies.com. In one way or another, they will all be used to allow me to continue to do what I have been doing for these past 23+ years. Please understand that I intend for Challies.com to always remain entirely free. In fact, patrons help ensure that it always remains that way. Thank you for considering becoming a patron of Challies.com. Your support means so much to me. And this is the end of my once-yearly mention of this subject! See Also Would You Consider Becoming a Patron? Would You Consider Becoming a Patron? Would You Consider Supporting My Work As a Patron?
content_zh:
我在Challies. 这一长期的承诺使我能够撰写数千篇文章和数百篇书评,同时通过每日的A La Carte专辑将数百万游客送到其他网站。

虽然我也写了很多书, 博客的许多内容现在也被翻译成西班牙语、法语和其他一些语言。 我最大的愿望之一是尽可能地自由奉献 我打算让它永远保持 完全自由的所有访问者。

我的目标是确保所有东西都能自由而广泛地分发。 虽然这在很大程度上是由于广告商造成的,但是个人的慷慨也可以发挥关键作用。 这里就是赞助人来的地方 像你这样的保镖 你们有几种不同的选择

第一种是每月反复提供的礼品。 一个名为Patreon的服务提供了一种将内容制作人(像我一样)与持续的支持者(像你一样)联系起来的方便手段. 你可以在Patreon.com/Challies上多学多学, 我还在那里每月分享部委和家庭的最新情况。 二是一次性赠送. 如果你感兴趣的话,它们可以通过PayPal以电子方式制作。

如果你愿意通过支票寄送一次性礼物,你可以简单地邮寄支票(在美国或加拿大银行挂牌)到这个地址: Tim Challies 1011 Upper Middle Road East, Box #1214 Oakville, 安大略省 L6H 5Z9 Canada 捐赠的资金将用于支持我的家庭,帮助创造伟大的内容或以其他方式改善,支持和增强Challies.com.

无论以何种方式,它们都将被用来允许我继续做我在过去23年多年中一直做的事情。 请理解我打算让Challies.com永远保持完全自由. 事实上,赞助者帮助确保它始终如此。 感谢您考虑成为Challies.com的赞助商. 你的支持对我很重要

summary_zh: 您可能面临的最艰难的一天/对于像我这样的人/向主宰历史的神祈祷/亲爱的α世代，Claude想把你们变成癞蛤蟆/老狗学新把戏/掌控我们的情绪/Kindle优惠等另请参阅A La Carte（4月24日）A La Carte（11月27日）A La Carte（11月22日）
title_zh: 单点菜肴（11月19日）
content: Thanks for reading A La Carte! I’ve got a good collection of articles, sales, deals, and other material for you this morning. I hope you enjoy it! Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a new edition of John Piper’s Desiring God , two reader-friendly studies in Romans from Tim Keller, The Gospel After Christendom , and my own From the Rising of the Sun (which, to remind you, includes the full documentary for free). Westminster Books is featuring my three Goers books for kids, each of which features a well-known Christian figure. They are nicely discounted. Logos users will want to check out Bible Study Week where you’ll find lots of deals, highlighted by the Tyndale OT & NT Commentaries at $4.99 each. Recommended Reading The Hardest Day You May Ever Face. This is a beautifully tragic piece of writing from Kimberly Wagner as she recounts an extremely hard day. “Daylight was just breaking over the ridge beyond the hills when I slipped into Mom’s bedroom and climbed into the bed beside her, the same bed that as a child I’d run to in the middle of the night to find safety and comfort. On this date, many years ago, we laid my dad’s body in the grave. But, Momma no longer remembers dates, or only guesses to know what season of the year we’re in. She won’t know the significance of today’s date, but she does have a foggy awareness that, to her today represents something terrible on her horizon.” For the Ones Like Me. Zachary Conover writes for those who are like him in that they were raised as good church kids. “What does it mean that we were dead in our trespasses and sins? How were we enemies of God? How were our hearts in rebellion against His Word? For students who have grown up attending church, reading the Bible, and learning about Jesus, these descriptions can be difficult to reconcile with their own experience. I understand that difficulty because I was one of those kids.” Praying to the God Who Rules History. Casey McCall reminds us that when we pray, we pray to the God who rules history. “If your doctrine of God leads you to pray less, you need to reevaluate your understanding of God. If your system of theology leads you to underemphasize the practical power of petitionary prayer in your life, you need to modify your system.” Dear Gen Alpha, Claude Wants to Turn You Into a Toad. Please, for the Love of All Things Human, Don’t Let It. Christina Bieber Lake warns members of Gen Alpha about what an all-out and unthoughtful commitment to Claude and other AI apps is likely to do to them. “In simple terms, we are moving from AI (Artificial Intelligence), which is about getting help processing information, to AGI (Artificial General Intelligence), which is about telling a machine what to do and letting it do it while you sit back and file your fingernails. Experts are saying that AGI will produce ten times the impact of the industrial revolution at ten times the speed.” Old Dogs and New Tricks. “I’m not opposed to the idea of people retiring after many decades of work. They have worked hard, so why not enjoy the fruit of their labor? But what I’ve found disquieting is the static nature that characterizes some retirements. I’ve seen some light, however, at the end of the tunnel and from where I stand, it doesn’t look like a train!” J.V. Fesko explains why he isn’t eager to retire, even if he does eventually withdraw from the front lines of work. Getting a Handle on Our Emotions. Writing for the Biblical Counseling Coalition, Esther St. John offers counsel on getting a handle on emotions, or, perhaps better said, stewarding them faithfully. A Great Error Respecting Duty I have often pointed out that Christians used to speak of duty far more often than we do today, since it was important to express and fulfill the duties God had given his people. You can read what William Plumer believed about duty in this brief quote from one of his works, A Word to the Weary . God’s people sometimes fall into a great error respecting their duty.
content_zh:
谢谢你读了《La Carte》! 今天早上我给你们收集了大量的文章、销售、交易和其他材料。 我希望你喜欢它!

他们被很好的折扣。 Logos 用户会想查看《圣经学习周》, 推荐阅读最难的一天 你永远希望面。 这是来自Kimberly Wagner的一部非常悲惨的作品,

" 日光刚从山上的山脊上冲过去,我滑进妈妈的卧室,爬到她旁边的床上,那张床就是小时候我半夜跑去寻找安全和舒适的床。 许多年前的这一天,我们把我父亲的尸体埋在坟墓里。 但妈妈不再记得日期,

她不会知道今天这个日子的意义, 但是她确实很困惑, Zachary Conover为那些像他一样的人写道, 他们被培养为教会的好孩子。 “我们因犯法和罪恶而死,这是什么意思? 我们是上帝的敌人吗?

我们的心如何违抗他的话? 对于在教堂里长大,阅读圣经,了解耶稣的学生来说,这些描述可能很难与自己的经历相协调. 我理解这种困难,因为我是那些孩子之一。” 向统治历史的上帝祈祷.

凯西·麦科尔提醒我们,当我们祈祷时,我们向统治历史的上帝祈祷. “如果你的神学引导你少祈祷,你就必须重新评价你对上帝的理解。 如果你的神学系统导致你低估了自己生活中请愿祈祷的实际力量,你需要修改你的系统。” 亲爱的阿尔法将军 克劳德想把你变成一只青蛙

“简言之,我们正在从AI(人工智能)转向AGI(人工智能),它涉及的是帮助处理信息,它涉及告诉机器该怎么做,让它做,而你却坐视不理,提交你的指甲。

专家说,AGI将以十倍的速度产生工业革命的十倍影响。” 老狗和新诡计。 “我不反对人们在工作几十年后退休。 他们辛勤工作,为什么不享受他们的劳动成果呢? 但我发现令人不安的是一些退休人士所特有的静态性。

但我看到隧道尽头有些灯光, J.V. Fesko解释为何他不急于退休, 得到一个处理 我们的情感。 为圣经咨询联盟撰稿 Esther St.

title: What Takes 20 Years to Build Takes 5 Minutes to Destroy
summary: I think we’ve all heard many variations of the adage, “It takes 20 years to build a reputation, but only five minutes to destroy it.” A good name that has been established through many years of honor, success, or skilled leadership can be ruined in a moment when an act of immorality comes to light. See Also A La Carte (2/13) The Sinner’s Opinion of Himself The True Character of Unbelief
summary_zh: 我想我们都听过这句话的各种版本：“建立声誉需要20年，但毁掉它只需要5分钟。” 经过多年荣誉、成功或出色领导而建立起来的好名声，在不道德行为曝光的那一刻就会毁于一旦。另见零散文章（2月13日）《罪人对自己的看法》《不信的真正本质》
title_zh: 花20年时间建造的东西，5分钟就能摧毁
content: I think we’ve all heard many variations of the adage, “It takes 20 years to build a reputation, but only five minutes to destroy it.” A good name that has been established through many years of honor, success, or skilled leadership can be ruined in a moment when an act of immorality comes to light. Until a couple of weeks ago, Jensen Huang seemed to be on top of the world. While Nvidia, the company he co-founded, had long been a Silicon Valley success story, the rise of AI had driven it to new heights of success and its CEO to new heights of prosperity. Nvidia became the most valuable company in the world, its market capitalization of nearly $6 trillion surpassing even Apple’s. Huang’s net worth soared to over $200 billion, making him one of the wealthiest men in the world and one of the richest men in history. His two children have advanced positions within the company and his wife of more than 40 years distributes vast sums of money through their charitable foundation. Huang carefully curated his reputation and, as is so often the case in Silicon Valley, his image, with his slick black leather jackets becoming his trademark. Today, of course, Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia or anything else. He was forced to resign after it came to light that he had engaged in extramarital affairs with multiple women, one of whom is allegedly a Chinese spy and another of whom is reportedly a subordinate within Nvidia. His image was shattered in a moment, and his reputation is now in tatters. The company lost over half a trillion dollars of value in the aftermath—value that was subtracted from Huang’s wealth, of course, but also from that of everyday investors whose wealth is far more modest. Pictures of his wife and children were splashed all over the news, and stories about his exploits were printed in every major media outlet in the world. The harm to his reputation is beyond repair, yet must pale in comparison to the harm and shame he has brought to his family. I hope that as Huang ponders what has become of his life, he has the wisdom to ask this: was it worth it? I hope each one of us asks the same, for Huang is not the first person to be tempted to grave sin , nor the first to succumb to temptation. In different ways and to different degrees, that is a battle we all fight every day. I have no experience of committing adultery, but I understand that it is exhilarating, and that doing what is forbidden delivers a great rush. And I suppose it must be exhilarating, for why else would a person risk so much to pursue it? Why else would a person do something that so defies common sense? Why else would a person gamble everything for the sake of illicit, fleeting pleasures? News reports describe him, in his final days at the company, calling himself “a piece of [expletive].” And while I wouldn’t phrase it that way, he’s not wrong that this situation has exposed him as what he truly is, and it’s actually far worse than the way he describes it. I might choose the word “wretch” to describe him, and not just him, but all of us. We are all wretches, for we are all wretched, people who trade short-term pleasure for long-term pain and fleeting joys for enduring sorrows. Sin makes us act like madmen, for sin is madness. And it leaves us wretched—desperately unhappy and in the sorriest of states. There has never been a sin that was more wise than foolish. There has never been a sin that delivered more gratification than the satisfaction of obedience. There has never been a sin that was worth more than the honor of a good name and an upstanding reputation. Thankfully, there has never been a sin that is beyond Jesus’s capacity to forgive. Though time and again we, like Huang, succumb to temptation, time and again Jesus forgives those who humble themselves before him to confess their sin and ask his forgiveness. May we all have the wisdom to see ourselves in Huang and to see in him a vivid example of the reality that sin promises joy while delivering sorr
content_zh:
我认为我们都听过许多不同的说法, “要建立名声需要20年, 一个通过多年的荣誉,成功,或熟练的领导而建立的良好名声,在不道德行为被揭发的一瞬间,可能会被破坏. 直到几周前,黄詹森似乎已经登上世界之巅.

虽然他共同创办的公司Nvidia长期是硅谷的成功故事,但是AI的崛起却将它推向了新的成功高地,其CEO也推向了新的繁荣高地. Nvidia成为了世界上最有价值的公司,其近6万亿美元的市场资本化甚至超过了苹果公司。

黄克诚的入股净值飙升至2000多亿美元,使他成为了世界上最富有的人之一,也是历史上最富有的人之一. 他的两个孩子在公司中担任高级职务,40多来年的妻子通过他们的慈善基金会发放一大笔钱.

黄克诚仔细地整理了自己的名声,并像硅谷经常出现的情况一样,他的形象被他浮出水面的黑色皮夹克也变成了他的商标. 今天,当然,黄已经不是恩维迪亚的首席执行官了

在得知他与多位妇女有婚外情后,他被迫辞职,其中一人据称是中国间谍,另一人据报是恩维迪亚的下属。 他的形象在一瞬间被打碎了,他的名声现在已经破灭了.

当然,该公司在事后损失了超过5万亿美元的价值 -- -- 当然,这一价值已经从黄家的财富中减去,同时也从日常投资者的财富中减去。 他妻子和孩子的相片被溅遍新闻,关于他剥削的故事被印入了世界上每一个主要的媒体渠道.

对他名誉的伤害是无法修复的,然而与他给家人带来的伤害和耻辱相比,必须苍白. 我希望,当黄帝思考他人生的结局时,他有智慧去问:这值得吗? 我希望我们每个人都问同样的问题 因为黄先生不是第一个 被严重罪孽诱惑的人 也不是第一个屈服于诱惑的人

以不同的方式和不同程度地,这是我们每天都要战斗的战斗。 我没有通奸的经验,但我明白,这是令人兴奋的,而做被禁止的事会带来极大的冲动。 我想这一定令人振奋 否则为什么一个人会冒险去追求呢? 否则一个人为什么要做 违背常识的事?

否则为什么一个人会赌取一切 为了非法的,短暂的快活? 新闻报导描述他在公司的最后几天自称是“一片[赞 ”。 虽然我并不会这样说, 但他并没有错误地认为这种情况暴露了他的真实面目,

我可能选择“错误”一词来形容他,而不仅仅是他,而是我们大家。 我们都是弱者,因为我们都是可怜人,他们以短期快活换取长期痛苦,以短暂的快活换取持久的悲伤。 罪恶让我们像疯子一样 因为罪恶就是疯狂 它使我们悲惨地 -- -- 极不幸福地 -- -- 在最烦恼的州里。

从未有过比愚蠢更明智的罪恶. 从来没有过罪过能带来比服从满足更多的满足. 从来没有一个罪过比一个好名声的荣誉和崇高的名声更值钱. 值得庆幸的是,从未有过耶稣无法宽恕的罪恶.

虽然我们像黄帝一样,一次又一次地屈从于诱惑,但耶稣一次又一次地原谅那些在他面前谦卑自卑的人,以忏悔他们的罪过并请求他的宽恕. 愿我们都有智慧去见自己在黄道上,在黄道上看到一个生动活泼的事例,说明罪恶许诺欢快,同时施以哀伤

content: Good morning, my friends. The God of love and peace be with you today. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a couple of daily Advent devotionals, Greg Koukl’s Street Smarts , David Gibson’s Living Life Backward , Dane Ortlund’s Deeper , and more. You’ll also find some academic titles from Zondervan Academic. If you prefer printed books, remember that there’s a big Pre-Black Friday sale happening now. I added lots of new books to the list yesterday. There are many great deals to be had! Recommended Reading Remembering John Allen Chau. P. R. Swain remembers and honors John Allen Chau. “There has been plenty of discussion around John’s level of wisdom and preparedness. Many feel these were lacking. I will admit that landing on an island whose inhabitants are known to be violent toward outsiders is unwise. The wiser thing would’ve been for him to invest his savings in a mutual fund for forty years. How short-sighted of him. In the words of one of the five in Ecuador who preceded him in martyrdom, ‘He is no fool who gives what he cannot keep to gain what he cannot lose.’ John was no fool.” How to Experience Gospel Transformation. This is a tremendous article from Nicholas McDonald on practicing repentance. “Here is my encouragement to you, as you learn to practice the prayer of reconciliation. Take 5-10 minutes each night, and try to choose one thing (not a million things) that needs repentance from your day. It’s very important that you go beyond just naming your sin to God, here. It’s important to name your sin (even out loud!), but that’s not going to transform you. What will transform you is learning to practice reconciliation with God, through the gospel.” The Quiet Voice. Catherine Mackenzie was one of those people who enjoyed the quiet that came to her life when Outlook crashed. “Although almost everything I had planned that day depended on email, and almost none of it got done, I actually talked to my colleagues. We caught up properly, in a way our inboxes don’t usually leave room for. I sat beside the designer instead of messaging her on Teams, and we all shared jokes and discussed our favourite period dramas.” She goes on to draw some observations from the marriage of John and Polly Newton. What We Get Wrong About the Tears of Jesus. John Piper addresses (and corrects, I suppose) a misplaced emphasis when it comes to a famous story from the life of Jesus—weeping outside the tomb of his friend Lazarus. I Thought Adultery Had Been Approved. David Hall writes about the downfall of Jensen Huang and the hypocrisy it unveils. “But, wait, is the NVDA board composed of pastors, puritans, and other assorted backwoods Baptists or something? I thought adultery had become widely acceptable. How can a company part with such a genius merely because of consensual sex out of marriage? Supposedly, this was a victimless crime that should not inhibit the rise of super duper intelligence, especially earning trillions.” The Singularity Will Never Happen. Some people are concerned that with the rise of AI we are heading to the point of singularity, but Justin Poythress explains why that will never happen. “We know the future will look dramatically different, but we’re only beginning to conceive the ways in which AI will reshape it. There is one thing Christians can know with certainty. It’s a knowledge which should equip Christians to lead the way in quelling the anxiety about this new world we’re hurtling toward. The Singularity … will never happen.” Videos Worth Watching What Is the Christian View of Suicide? Kevin DeYoung answers a common question during a Q&A. 50 Difficult Theology Questions Answered in 50 Minutes . Adriel Sanchez answers a whole lot of questions in a short format. Among them are questions like these: Is America in the end times? Why are there so many different denominations? Are Mormons and Catholics Christians? Why does evil exist in the world? Why Does Jesus Speak in Parables? Daniel Stevens explains why Jesus rel

summary_zh: 上帝有时会选择出人意料的道路，引导每个人走向自己的天职。现年 72 岁的比尔·罗兹（Bill Rhodes）的人生就是一个很好的例子。26 岁时，这位美国人在圣地的公路上意外邂逅，彻底改变了他的命运。就在几年前，他还从事着体力劳动。没有任何迹象表明他注定要成为一名外科医生，更不用说将自己一生的大部分时间奉献给穷人了。
title_zh: 比尔·罗兹（Bill Rhodes）：因搭车客而从工人成为外科医生的传奇人物
content: Dieu emprunte parfois des chemins inattendus pour conduire chacun vers sa vocation. La vie de Bill Rhodes, aujourd’hui âgé de 72 ans, en est une belle illustration. À 26 ans, une rencontre inattendue sur une route de Terre sainte bouleverse le destin de cet Américain qui, quelques années plus tôt, exerçait encore des métiers manuels. Rien ne le prédestinait à devenir chirurgien, encore moins à consacrer une grande partie de son existence aux populations les plus pauvres d’Afrique. Pourtant, depuis près de trois décennies, c’est au Kenya, dans un hôpital isolé, qu’il met ses compétences médicales au service des plus démunis, guidé par sa foi profonde en Jésus-Christ. Tout commence dans les années 1970. Élevé dans une famille non croyante, Bill Rhodes découvre le Christ dans sa jeunesse, presqu’en même temps qu’il fait connaissance de Laura qui deviendra son épouse. Ils se marient rapidement : il n’a alors que 20 ans et elle, 19. « Je ne manifestais aucun intérêt particulier Tout lire… The post Bill Rhodes, l’ouvrier devenu chirurgien grâce à un auto-stoppeur appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
上帝有时会走意想不到的道路，引导每个人找到自己的使命。现年 72 岁的比尔·罗兹（Bill Rhodes）的人生就是一个很好的例子。26岁时，这位美国人在圣地的公路上意外邂逅，从此改变了他的命运。就在几年前，他还从事着体力劳动。

没有任何迹象表明他注定会成为一名外科医生，更不用说将自己一生的大部分时间奉献给非洲最贫困的群体。然而，近三十年来，他一直身处肯尼亚的一家偏远医院，在对耶稣基督的深厚信仰的指引下，将自己的医学技能用于为最贫困的人群服务。这一切始于 20 世纪 70 年代。

比尔·罗兹（Bill Rhodes）成长于一个非信徒家庭，他在年轻时认识了基督，几乎与此同时，他也结识了后来成为他妻子的劳拉（Laura）。他们很快就结婚了：当时他才20岁，她19岁。“我并没有表现出特别的兴趣……阅读全文……文章《比尔·罗兹：因一位搭便车者而从工人成为外科医生的男人》最初发表于Aleteia网站。”

title: « Le Clair-Obscur d’Emmaüs », dialogue imaginaire entre Malraux et Arcabas
summary: Il y a cent ans naissait Arcabas, et il y cinquante ans, mourrait André Malraux. title_zh: 《“以马忤斯”的光影效果》，马尔罗与阿尔卡巴斯之间的虚构对话
content: Il y a cent ans naissait Arcabas, et il y cinquante ans, mourrait André Malraux. Ce double anniversaire m’a inspiré d’écrire un dialogue imaginaire entres ces deux créateurs fascinants, ne s’étant pas rencontrés de leur vivant. Tous deux sont taraudés par la question du sens et de la spiritualité. Pour le peintre chrétien, elle était la pointe de sa créativité. Pour l’écrivain agnostique, elle était une interrogation primordiale.  Arcabas (1926-2018) s’appelait de son vrai nom Jean-Marie Pirot. Il est un peintre, sculpteur et maître verrier français emblématique de l’art sacré contemporain. Natif de Moselle, il fut professeur aux Beaux-Arts de Grenoble. Il adopta le pseudonyme Arcabas à la fin des années 1960 pour marquer un tournant dans sa carrière artistique. Il lui avait été inspiré par un graffiti étudiant vu sur un mur lors des manifestations de Mai 68. Son style, reconnaissable à ses couleurs éclatantes et à son usage de l’or, mêle figuration et abstraction pour exprimer une foi Tout lire… The post « Le Clair-Obscur d’Emmaüs », dialogue imaginaire entre Malraux et Arcabas appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
一百年前，阿尔卡巴斯（Arcabas）出生；五十年前，安德烈·马尔罗（André Malraux）去世。这两个周年纪念日启发我撰写了一段这两位迷人的艺术家之间的虚构对话，他们生前从未谋面。两人都为意义和精神层面的问题所困扰。对于这位基督画家来说，这个问题是他创作力的巅峰。

对于这位不可知论作家来说，这是一个至关重要的问题。阿尔卡巴斯（1926-2018）的真名叫让-玛丽·皮罗（Jean-Marie Pirot）。他是一位法国画家、雕塑家和玻璃工艺大师，是当代宗教艺术的标志性人物。他出生于摩泽尔省，曾任格勒诺布尔美术学院教授。

20 世纪 60 年代末，他开始使用笔名“Arcabas”，以标志其艺术生涯的转折点。这个笔名源自他在 1968 年 5 月的示威活动中在墙上看到的一幅学生涂鸦。

他的风格以鲜艳的色彩和对金色的运用而闻名，将具象与抽象相结合，以表达对信仰的深刻理解。阅读全文……文章《“以马忤斯的明暗对比”：马尔罗与阿尔卡巴斯之间的虚构对话》最初发表于Aleteia。
author: Michel Cool

title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
summary_zh: 我是来自古利内的西门。 我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. content_zh:
我是来自古利内的西门。我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。尽管如此，我的皮肤并不黑，嘴唇也不厚。尽管我的家族已经在昔兰尼生活了几代人，昔兰尼是昔兰尼加的首府，这是一座位于北非的希腊城市，以其繁荣和哲学家而闻名，但我的肤色并不白。我是古利奈的西门。

我从心底里是一个地道的犹太人。从小到大，我毫无例外地遵守所有宗教律法，尽管由于在讲希腊语的社区长大，我已经不再精通阿拉姆语。我是古利奈人西门。我不想谈论我自己。也不想讲述我所有的生活经历。我只想讲述我那一次的经历。

这段经历后来改变了我的人生轨迹。如果您也经历过，那么也会改变您的人生轨迹。那天是星期五。那天早上我刚抵达耶路撒冷。我长途跋涉的目的就是为了庆祝逾越节。我每年都这样做。看到熙熙攘攘的人群挤满了这座城市，我一点也不感到惊讶。

尽管很累，但在酒店放下行李并洗漱完毕后，我还是出门散步，享受这座沉浸在节日气氛中的城市的喧嚣。

到处跑来跑去的孩子们尖叫声，叫卖的小贩们劝诱甚至有时强迫的吆喝声，还有熏香的味道或人们吟唱赞美诗的悠扬声音——这一切都让我忘记了疲惫。这种略显喧闹的氛围与古利奈文雅有序的氛围截然不同，但却更有活力。

突然间，出现了一阵不寻常的喧哗。罗马士兵挤过人群。“唉，又是罗马士兵的游行，用来提醒人们谁才是这个国家的统治者。”我想。但是不是。在最前面一排，有一名士兵拿着一面旗帜，上面写着：“拿撒勒人耶稣，犹太人的王。” 我确实从未见过祂。

但是，“耶稣”这个名字，谁不认识他呢？他是最具争议的人物。我不明白的是，为什么罗马士兵要举着这样的旗帜游行。因此，我走近仔细观察。在罗马士兵的方阵中间，有三个人背着十字架缓缓前行。“大坏蛋，”我想。不过，这和那面旗帜有什么关系？

然后我渐渐明白了。人群喧嚣着，一边喊着耶稣的名字，一边嘲笑祂。还有不少人向祂吐唾沫。但是，这三个人当中哪一个是耶稣呢？我是古利奈人西门。我走得越来越近。然后我确切地知道谁是耶稣。他是三人中个子最小的，几乎没有肌肉。

祂的长发散乱，这里那里都沾满了干涸的血迹，这些血迹来自祂头上戴着的荆棘冠。祂的全身都瘀青了。祂的步伐蹒跚。祂非常疲惫。但是祂的眼睛——尽管因为睡眠不足而发红——但每次注视时仍然锐利如刀。奇怪的是，他的眼神也如此温柔、令人舒心。我无法移开视线，不去看祂的眼睛。

充满威严，但也非常平和和慈父般。然后祂倒下了。祂瘦小而几乎破碎的身体再也承受不住肩上十字架的重量。人群像嗜血的野兽一样欢呼雀跃。鞭子抽打着祂的背。鲜血喷涌而出。祂又慢慢地站了起来。祂疲惫不堪。但是祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

然后他走了几步。然而，祂又倒下了。游行队伍停了下来。人群变得越来越凶狠。鞭子一次又一次地挥舞着。鲜血喷涌而出。然而，祂再也无法站起来了。我是古利奈人西门。不知为何，这一切并没有真正触动我。除了祂的眼神。祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

因此，当一名士兵突然拉我时，我好像失去了知觉。然后把十字架放在我身上。

title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）

summary_zh: 我叫 Martin Kilonzo 神父，ALCP/OSS。我是一名罗马天主教神父，也是圣神工团体（Opus Spiritus Sancti，简称ALCP/OSS）的司铎宗徒生活团体成员。我来自东非的肯尼亚，
title_zh: 隆重介绍圣若瑟天主教堂助理神父马丁·基隆佐（Martin Kilonzo）
content: My name is Fr. Martin Kilonzo, ALCP/OSS. I am a Roman Catholic priest and a member of the Apostolic Life Community of Priests in Opus Spiritus Sancti (ALCP/OSS). Originally from Kenya, East Africa, I currently serve as parochial vicar at St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, N.D. My journey has been a remarkable experience of faith, formation, missionary service, and trust in God’s providence. I was born in 1978 in Kilenge, a small village in Makueni County, southeastern Kenya, where I attended elementary school. I later joined Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary in the Diocese of Machakos, my home diocese, where I received a high school education and spiritual formation that helped prepare me for the priesthood. After four years at the minor seminary, I pursued three years of philosophical studies at the Spiritan Missionary Seminary in Arusha, Tanzania, followed by four years of theological studies at Jordan University College in Morogoro, Tanzania. I was ordained a priest in July 2012 in the Diocese of Moshi, in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro Region. Since my ordination, I have served in various pastoral assignments in Tanzania and Italy, enriching my missionary experience and understanding of different cultures. In 2026, following consultations between my religious superiors and the Bishop of Fargo, I was assigned to the Diocese of Fargo, N.D., beginning a new chapter in my priestly ministry. October 15 holds special significance for me as the anniversary of the day I first set foot on American soil. I arrived in Chicago before taking a connecting flight to Minot, N.D. After spending approximately one week serving at St. Mary’s Cathedral in Fargo, I was assigned to St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, where I officially began my ministry as parochial vicar in February 2026. I consider my assignment in North Dakota a privilege and a renewed call to missionary service. Through God’s grace, I am grateful for the opportunity to celebrate the sacraments, provide spiritual guidance, and serve the parishioners of St. Joseph’s Church and the wider Devils Lake community, regardless of religious affiliation or background. For me, the journey from Kilenge, Kenya, to Devils Lake, N.D., is more than a change of place; it is a continuing response to God’s call to faith, service, and missionary discipleship with humility.

我叫马丁・基隆佐,ALCP/OSS。 我是一名罗马天主教神父,也是奥普斯·斯皮里图斯·桑茨蒂(ALCP/OSS)牧师的使徒生活社区的成员。 我最初来自肯尼亚、东非, 我的旅程在信仰、组织、传教仪式和对上帝之赐的信任方面,是非凡的经历。

1978年出生于肯尼亚东南部马库埃尼县的一个小村庄Kilenge,在那里就读小学. 我后来加入教宗保罗六世小神学院(Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary),参加我的家乡教区马查科斯教区,在那里我接受了高中教育和精神培养,帮助我为神职做好准备.

在小神学院学习了四年之后,我在坦桑尼亚阿鲁沙的Spiritan传教士神学院学习了三年哲学,之后在坦桑尼亚莫罗戈罗的约旦大学学院学习了四年神学。 我于2012年7月在坦桑尼亚乞力马扎罗大区莫希教区被任命为牧师。

自从我担任教职以来,我在坦桑尼亚和意大利从事各种牧业任务,丰富了我的传教经验和对不同文化的理解。 2026年,经我的宗教上司与法尔戈主教磋商,我被分配到北大法尔戈主教座堂,开始了我牧师部的新篇章.

10月15日是我第一次踏上美国土地的纪念日,对我来说具有特殊的意义. 我在搭乘连接航班去纽约州米诺特之前到达芝加哥 在法戈的圣玛丽大教堂服役约一周后,我被分配到魔鬼湖的圣约瑟教堂,2026年2月正式开始我的牧师部。

我将我在北达科他州的任务视为一种特权,也是对传教士服务的再次呼吁。 通过上帝的恩典,我感谢有机会庆祝圣训,提供精神指导,并为圣约瑟教堂的教友和更广泛的恶魔湖社区服务,而不论其宗教信仰或背景如何.

对我而言,从肯尼亚基伦格到N.D.D.的恶魔湖的旅程不仅仅是改变地方;它是对上帝发出的信仰、服务和谦逊的传教士的不断响应。
